glance: OpenAI proposed perplexity as a shared metric for pacing frontier AI, a canary test exposed prompt leaks across inference providers, and a Dutch court blocked BYD's Ti7 in the EU over Land Rover design rights. Euro 7 takes effect for new car types this week, Stellantis is set to quit works racing, and Chinese brands keep pushing into Europe despite thinner margins.
brief: Good morning. Here is Vertical News for Monday the twenty-third of November, covering the weekend. OpenAI's chief scientist, Jakub Pachocki, has proposed perplexity, a measure of how well a model predicts text, as a shared yardstick for frontier AI. OpenAI published its own figures for the first time and asked rival labs to agree common limits until better safety monitoring exists. A canary test by the security firm Dragos caught AI inference providers leaking prompts, and seeded cloud keys were later used by attackers. OpenRouter dropped three providers and pulled a hundred and twenty-five endpoints from its zero-retention list. And a Dutch court has barred BYD from selling or building its Ti7 in the EU, after Jaguar Land Rover argued it copies the Defender design. BYD will appeal. In other news, the Lean community says the Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis checks out formally. UN talks on autonomous weapons ended without a mandate to negotiate a ban. Cursor told US lawmakers it may phase out Chinese open-weight models. Lovable added new models, payment connectors and company-only publishing. Google added EU data-region controls and an AI switch to Workspace Studio. In automotive, Stellantis is reported to be ending its works racing programmes. Euro 7 applies to new car types from Sunday, including the first brake-dust limits. Leapmotor's profit fell seventy-three percent even as its platform launched in Europe under Hongqi. Volkswagen is finally fixing the PerfektBlue Bluetooth flaws. And in research, a UK and Chinese study shows crowded trains can cut wheelset crack-growth life by up to seventy-two percent.

stories.headline: OpenAI's chief scientist proposes perplexity as a shared yardstick for frontier AI and publishes OpenAI's own figures
stories.why: If labs agree common limits on training progress, release pacing of the models your products depend on could become an industry-wide negotiation.
body: Jakub Pachocki, OpenAI's chief scientist, published an essay on Sunday arguing that perplexity, a measure of how well a model predicts held-out text, should become a common metric for tracking frontier progress. For the first time OpenAI released its internal pretraining log-perplexity on a held-out code dataset: about 0.99 for GPT-3.5, about 0.91 for GPT-4, and below 0.8 for the models where strong cyber-security and maths abilities appeared. A model at about 0.76 began producing notable results on open maths problems, and he expects further, unknown jumps around 0.68 to 0.70.

He proposes that frontier labs agree shared evaluation norms, transparency standards and common limits tied to measures like perplexity, not to be crossed until monitoring milestones are met, such as a successor to chain-of-thought monitors. He warns that AI-driven pretraining research could cause a sudden burst of progress, possibly as soon as 2027, and admits the metric's weaknesses: labs train on different data and the number does not map to specific tasks.

For Europe the proposal lands next to the AI Act's rules for general-purpose models with systemic risk, which also need measurable thresholds. The next test is whether Anthropic, Google and others publish comparable numbers.

stories.headline: Canary test catches AI inference providers leaking prompts, and OpenRouter drops three of them
stories.why: Teams routing model calls through aggregators cannot rely on zero-retention flags alone; prompts with customer data or secrets may be exposed.
body: Security firm Dragos sent about two million prompts containing seeded web addresses and credentials through AI inference services between July and November, tracing roughly 2,000 routes. Several hundred passed through systems it could not identify. Attackers stole data from three hosting providers, and about 200 seeded AWS keys planted in late October were later used for tens of thousands of AWS API calls. None of the providers knew until Dragos told them. On one marketplace, sellers could see and keep customer prompts through ordinary request logging, and zero-retention settings appeared to be ignored.

On Sunday OpenRouter removed three unnamed providers and took 125 endpoints off its zero-data-retention list, some as a precaution, and said it will keep running similar tests. Provider notices describe misrouted MiniMax requests at Novita, an attacker controlling a virtual machine serving DeepSeek traffic at Phala, and an AI coding agent at Together AI that pushed a credential to public GitHub.
For product teams this is a GDPR and supply-chain issue: pin the providers you trust, avoid secrets in prompts, and rotate any keys that may have passed through third-party inference.

stories.headline: Dutch court bars BYD from selling or building the Ti7 in the EU over Land Rover Defender design rights
stories.why: Registered design rights are becoming a tool for European OEMs against Chinese entrants, and this ruling reaches BYD's Hungarian plant.
body: The preliminary relief judge at the District Court of The Hague granted Jaguar Land Rover a temporary injunction on Friday, finding that BYD's Ti7 plug-in hybrid likely infringes the Defender 110 design JLR registered in the EU in 2018. The order covers importing, manufacturing and delivering the Ti7 anywhere in the EU, including at BYD's new plant in Hungary. It takes effect a week after formal service, with penalties capped at 10 million euros.

JLR must start a full case on the merits within six months or the injunction may lapse. The UK is not covered, because the court said it had no jurisdiction over BYD's UK arm, where deliveries are planned from January 2027. BYD says it strongly disagrees and will appeal. The seven-seat Ti7 is not yet on sale in the EU but has sold more than 300,000 units in China.

The ruling reverses the direction of earlier rounds, when the same court ordered JLR to destroy documents seized from BYD. For design and engineering teams, it is a reminder that exterior design registrations carry real commercial weight in Europe.

stories.headline: Lean community certifies the Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
stories.why: Machine-checked verification at this scale is a model for how to trust AI-generated work in other high-stakes fields, including engineering sign-off.
body: A joint statement on the Lean community blog, endorsed by the Lean Focused Research Organization and the Mathlib Initiative, says the formal proof of the Riemann Hypothesis released by Levent Alpöge on Friday checks out. The library is about 17 million lines of Lean and depends only on Mathlib, the community's shared maths library. Dozens of people reproduced the same compiled proof export.

Two tools confirmed that the proved theorem matches Mathlib's vetted statement of the Riemann Hypothesis, so the proof cannot have quietly proved something easier. Several independent proof checkers, including Lean's own kernel and checkers written in other languages, accepted it. The checks ran on an inert export, so hidden code in the proof sources could not interfere. Emergent reports that more than 175,000 modules compiled with no errors in about 24 hours.

This is a community certification, not journal peer review, and mathematicians still need to understand the ideas. But it shows a workable pattern: when AI produces something too large for people to read, independent machine checking against an agreed specification can establish that it is correct.

stories.headline: UN talks on autonomous weapons end without a mandate to negotiate a ban
stories.why: There will be no binding international rules on autonomous weapons before 2028 at the earliest, which matters for Europe's dual-use autonomy suppliers.
body: The review conference of the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons ended in Geneva early on Saturday without agreeing to negotiate a legally binding instrument on lethal autonomous weapons. Nearly 100 of the 128 states attending backed negotiations, but the conference works by consensus, and the United States was among those opposed. Russia had earlier called restrictions premature.

The compromise asks government experts to develop elements of an instrument by 2028 and then propose whether it should become a binding treaty. During the week the US had proposed five years of talks on a non-binding text, while the Peruvian chair suggested a draft binding protocol by 2028. Campaign groups including Stop Killer Robots called the result the lowest common denominator.

For European companies working on perception, autonomy and robotics with possible defence uses, the outcome means national export rules and the EU's own frameworks remain the main constraints for several more years.

stories.headline: Cursor tells US lawmakers it may phase out Chinese open-weight models
stories.why: Model provenance is turning into a procurement and compliance question for any product built on Qwen, Kimi or DeepSeek.
body: A report from the US House Homeland Security Committee and the Select Committee on China, released on Friday, says Cursor will explore phasing out Chinese-developed open-weight models, with no decision or timetable. Cursor's flagship Composer 2 model is built on Moonshot's Kimi K2.5, which the committees note became public only after an outside developer spotted it.

The inquiry also looked at Airbnb and DoorDash. Airbnb runs customised Alibaba Qwen models on US servers, with one assistant handling about 80,000 guest and host conversations a day. DoorDash reported 25 Chinese model families in use and said replacing one embedded in a larger system could take up to six months. The committees recommend extending the federal DeepSeek ban to other Chinese developers, barring such models from federal contracts and critical infrastructure, and creating a model-provenance standard, while warning against removing them before trusted alternatives exist.
European teams that rely on Chinese open-weight models, directly or through tools, should expect customers to ask what is inside their stack and be ready to answer.

stories.headline: Lovable adds GPT-6.2 models, new payment connectors and publishing to a company email domain
stories.why: Prompt-to-app tools are moving from prototypes to paid and internally deployed apps, which changes how design and product teams hand off and govern work.
body: Swedish prompt-to-app builder Lovable updated its platform on Friday. Apps built with it can now call OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra for complex reasoning and GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday tasks, both with text and image input. New connectors for Square and for Paystack, which covers Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa and Côte d'Ivoire, follow Adyen and Airwallex connectors added the day before.

Enterprise customers can now publish an app to a verified company email domain, so anyone with that address can open it after logging in. That turns Lovable into a way to ship internal tools without a separate hosting and access setup. Paid web plans also get a free domain for the first year.

The direction is clear: payments, access control and model choice are being built in, so what starts as a prototype can run as a real product. For design and product teams, that raises questions about who reviews and maintains these apps once they go live, especially after recent reports of Lovable-built apps exposing data.

stories.headline: Google adds EU data-region controls and an AI switch for Workspace Studio
stories.why: Data residency plus an admin on/off switch for generative AI is what many EU companies need before enabling agent workflows.
body: Google says the core features of Workspace Studio, its tool for building automated flows and agents, now follow US or EU data-region policies, and that support is generally available. A new admin control decides whether users in a data region may use generative AI. When it is off, Studio's AI steps, flow generation from plain language and Skills are disabled; both this control and the Gemini in Workspace setting must be on for AI to work.

In the same update, client-side encrypted Google Docs gain real-time co-editing in beta, with encryption keys staying under the customer's control. Gemini Enterprise also made third-party data stores generally available, including Asana, Airtable, GitLab, Stripe, Zapier and Linear.

For product leaders, this is a pattern worth copying: AI features in business software increasingly ship with region-level data residency and a separate, explicit AI toggle for administrators, so compliance teams can approve the product before approving the AI.

stories.headline: Stellantis is reported to be ending all works motorsport, with works councils meeting today
stories.why: Europe's second-largest carmaker is cutting a high-end test bed for hybrid powertrains as part of its cost programme.
stories.source: Sportscar365 · Le Figaro via Global Banking & Finance · Autonext
body: Le Figaro reported on Friday that Stellantis will close its works racing programmes: Peugeot's Hypercar entry in the World Endurance Championship and the Citroën and Opel teams in Formula E. Two extraordinary works-council meetings with Stellantis Motorsport staff are set for Monday at Poissy and Satory. Peugeot confirmed the meetings but would not comment on the substance.

Monday is also the closing date for 2027 WEC entries, so withdrawing now could avoid penalties. About 300 people work at Stellantis Motorsport near Versailles. Peugeot's WEC programme is estimated to cost more than 30 million euros a year, and its 9X8 has not won a race since its 2022 debut. The context is a savings programme of 6 billion euros by 2028.

For engineers, works racing has long served as a fast development loop for hybrid systems, energy management and simulation methods. Losing it shows how hard the cost squeeze at European OEMs has become. Official confirmation is expected today.

stories.headline: Euro 7 applies to new car and van types from Sunday, with the first brake-dust limits
stories.why: Brake-particle and battery-durability testing become part of type approval, directly affecting brake, test, simulation and cell teams.
body: From 29 November, new type approvals for cars and vans in the EU must meet Euro 7, and from 29 November 2027 all newly registered cars and vans must comply. Buses and trucks follow with new types from 29 May 2028. Tailpipe limits stay close to Euro 6, but particle counting now goes down to 10 nanometres instead of 23.

The bigger change is outside the exhaust. Brake particle limits are set at 7 milligrams per kilometre for combustion, hybrid and fuel-cell cars and 3 for battery-electric cars, with tyre abrasion limits to follow through UN rules. Durability requirements rise to 10 years or 200,000 kilometres. Electric and plug-in hybrid batteries must keep at least 80 percent of certified energy after five years or 100,000 kilometres, and 72 percent after eight years or 160,000 kilometres. On-board emissions monitoring becomes mandatory.
For test and validation teams, this means new brake-emission test procedures, longer durability evidence, and battery-ageing models that must stand up in homologation.

stories.headline: Leapmotor's revenue rises 63% but profit falls 73%, as its platform launches in Europe under Hongqi
stories.why: The fastest-growing Chinese brand in Europe is feeling cost pressure, while its platform now reaches European buyers through a second Chinese group.
body: Leapmotor, Stellantis's Chinese partner, reported unaudited third-quarter revenue of 31.7 billion yuan, up 63 percent, on a record 310,052 deliveries. Net profit fell 73 percent to 40 million yuan and gross margin dropped to 10.9 percent from 14.5 percent a year earlier, which the company blames on raw-material costs, product mix and higher shipping costs. Exports rose to 63,278 cars, about a fifth of volume.

On the same day, FAW's Hongqi launched the EHS4 electric SUV in Europe, built on Leapmotor's LEAP 3.5 platform. Italy is the first market, with introductory prices from 32,900 euros. It has a 160 kW rear motor and a 68.7 kWh LFP battery integrated into the chassis, giving up to 460 km WLTP and charging at up to 178 kW on a 400 V system. Hongqi plans ten models for Europe next year.
Platform sharing between Chinese groups is now reaching Europe at Volkswagen ID.3 prices, while thinner margins suggest the price war has limits.

stories.headline: Volkswagen ID.4 owners get a fix for the PerfektBlue Bluetooth flaws about two years after the supplier patch
stories.why: A concrete case of how slowly supplier software fixes reach cars in the field, relevant to every team working under UN R155 and R156.
body: Volkswagen is rolling out fixes for the four PerfektBlue vulnerabilities in OpenSynergy's BlueSDK Bluetooth stack, which researchers at PCA Cyber Security reported in May 2024. OpenSynergy patched the stack in September 2024, so the vehicle-side fix comes roughly 26 months later. The worst flaw has a severity score of 8.0. The researchers tested Volkswagen's MEB infotainment unit, Mercedes NTG6 and Škoda MIB3.

The attack works within about ten metres but needs someone in the car to accept a pairing request. In tests the researchers reportedly controlled heating, wipers and the sunroof and recorded audio through the eCall microphone, with no evidence of access to brakes, steering or driver assistance. Volkswagen's route depends on software version: an over-the-air update for 3.x cars, a dealer visit for 4.x, an online update for some 5.x versions. Volkswagen says safety was never at risk and is not writing to owners.
For software-defined-vehicle teams, the gap between supplier patch and fleet fix is the real risk to manage.

stories.headline: Crowded trains cut predicted crack-growth life of high-speed wheelsets by up to 72%, mainly through load variability
stories.why: Inspection intervals and load spectra for axles, shafts and bearing seats should follow load variability and overload cases, not mean load.
body: Researchers at Shijiazhuang Tiedao University in China and the Institute of Railway Research at the University of Huddersfield in the UK published a peer-reviewed study in Lubricants on how passenger load affects fatigue in a high-speed railway wheelset. They combined a vehicle-dynamics model with a finite-element wheelset model that includes the press fit between wheel and axle, counted load cycles with rainflow counting, summed damage with Miner's rule, and modelled a semi-elliptical surface crack.

Compared with an empty train, maximum fatigue damage was about 9, 20 and 102 times higher for seated, fully laden and crush-laden cases, and predicted crack-growth life fell by up to 72 percent. Under crush load, the mean vertical force rose only 19 percent, but the spread of suspension forces was almost three times larger. The groove next to the wheel seat was the critical location in every case.
The lesson carries over to driveshafts and bearing seats: overload and variability, not average load, drive damage, and press-fit transitions are where ultrasonic inspection should focus.

watch.title: SKF Vertevo listing
watch.text: The last day to trade SKF with the right to Vertevo shares is 25 November, and the automotive business starts trading on Nasdaq Stockholm on 1 December, one Vertevo share for every five SKF shares.

watch.title: US–China AI guardrails
watch.text: Trump said the US would work with China on joint guardrails for AI, according to Semafor. No scope or timetable has been given.

watch.title: Volkswagen pay talks
watch.text: Volkswagen and IG Metall open talks in Emden on 24 November, with a second round in Zwickau on 15 December, after the carmaker asked for a two-year pay freeze.
